title: Emerging Personas and Tools for Hybrid Quantum-HPC Systems
authors: Eun-Kyung Lee, Jessie Yu, Claudio Carvalho, Yoonho Park, Marcelo Amaral, Tim Osborne, Woong Shin
abstract: Quantum computing is entering an era where quantum processing units (QPUs) with tens to hundreds of qubits are increasingly integrated with high-performance computing (HPC) systems to support hybrid quantum-classical workloads. This paradigm, often referred to as Quantum-Centric SuperComputing (QCSC), introduces new operational, software, and infrastructure challenges. In this paper, we identify and characterize six distinct personas involved in QCSC environments. Particular attention is given to emerging roles that arise at the interface between quantum and HPC systems. We analyze the responsibilities and tools associated with each persona and examine their differing requirements for operational data. Consistent data representations and analytics frameworks will be required to support diverse users across the quantum-HPC ecosystem. By defining personas and their data needs, we provide a foundation for future discussions in this critical area.
summary: This paper addresses the operational challenges of integrating quantum processors with supercomputers, creating the concept of Quantum-Centric Supercomputing (QCSC). It achieves this by identifying and detailing six distinct user personas, each with unique tools and data requirements. The core contribution is establishing a framework based on these personas to guide the development of standardized data formats for the entire quantum-HPC ecosystem.
main_problem: The primary challenge is operationalizing Quantum-Classical Supercomputing (QCSC) by managing the complex integration of Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) with High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems.
main_result: The paper argues that defining distinct user personas and understanding their specific data needs is crucial for developing the necessary consistent data representations and analytics frameworks for the entire quantum-HPC ecosystem.
method: The authors characterize six distinct user personas involved in QCSC environments, analyzing their responsibilities, required tools, and operational data needs.
model_or_system: The focus is on the conceptual framework of Quantum-Centric Supercomputing (QCSC) systems, which integrate QPUs (tens to hundreds of qubits) with classical HPC infrastructure.
key_observables: Operational data, system health, resource utilization, circuit fidelity, and time-to-solution are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: The scale of integration (tens to hundreds of qubits) and the need for unified resource management are critical.
main_assumptions: The paper assumes that a single term like 'quantum user' is insufficient, necessitating a persona-based approach to system design.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview of six quantum user personas and their relationship to the layered QCSC architecture, while Table I lists the tools associated with each persona.
paper_structure: The paper identifies the QCSC problem, characterizes the six user personas, analyzes their roles and tools, and concludes by stressing the need for standardized data representations to support the diverse user base.
why_interesting: It provides a high-level, systems-engineering perspective on the practical challenges of quantum hardware integration, which informs the necessary software and data infrastructure for future quantum simulation work.
